								<section id="section-1785874388" class="tab" data-animation="fadeIn"><div class="infi-content-wrapper"><p>Joe Lycett<span style="font-weight: 400;"> is an award-winning comedian, writer, artist and television host.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">A hugely successful and acclaimed stand up comedian, Joe has extensively toured across the UK and internationally. He has produced 3 specials from his sell out international tours: </span><b>That’s The Way, A-Ha A-Ha, Joe Lycett</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (2016);  </span><b>I’m About To Lose Control And I Think Joe Lycett</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (2018) and </span><b>More, More, More! How Do You Lycett? How Do You Lycett? </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">(2023). His last show took in arenas and theatres across the UK and Ireland in 2022, followed by an Australian and New Zealand leg in early 2023. In total, the tour was seen live by over 200,000 people. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Currently, Joe can be seen live at a mixed bill show he hosts called <strong>Joe Lycett & Friends</strong>, which following a 2025 residency at the Birmingham Glee Club, pops up at various venues across the UK. Joe is taking this format up to the Edinburgh Fringe this August. Most recently, he announced his latest UK national tour for 2027-2028, <strong>Do You Really Lycett? Is It Is, It Wicked? We’re Lovin’ It, Lovin’ It, Lovin’ It, We’re Lovin’ It Lycett</strong>.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Joe is an award-winning and highly regarded TV host; his work has won him two <strong>BAFTA</strong>s, two <strong>Royal Television Society Awards</strong> plus<strong> Rose D’or</strong> and <strong>Grierson</strong> nominations. His latest show, recently announced for later this year on Channel 4, is <strong>The Lycett Arms</strong>. The topical comedy show, with Joe has host, will air live from a pub in London on Friday nights. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Joe has also presented a Sky series, <strong>Joe Lycett’s United States of Birmingham </strong>(Sky), which followed him uniting eighteen Birminghams across North America. </span><span style="font-weight: 400;">Joe hosted several series of his own live TV show </span><b>Late Night Lycett</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (C4) in his hometown of Birmingham. He fronted his own comedy consumer affairs show </span><b>Joe Lycett’s Got Your Back </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">(C4) and is also the host of Channel 4’s long-running travel documentary series, </span><b>Travel Man</b><span style="font-weight: 400;">. He hosted several series of </span><b>The Great British Sewing Bee</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (BBC), presented <b>Joe Lycett: Summer Exhibitionist </b>as part of the BBC’s coverage of the Royal Academy Summer Exhibition in 2022</span><span style="font-weight: 400;"> as well as hosting Channel 4’s </span><b>Joe Lycett’s Big Pride Party</b><span style="font-weight: 400;">. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Joe’s special </span><b>Joe Lycett vs The Oil Giant</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> was nominated for a </span><b>Grierson Award</b><span style="font-weight: 400;">. In 2022, Channel 4 aired a </span><b>Joe Lycett vs David Beckham: Got Your Back at Xmas, </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">which won a </span><b>BAFTA </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">and a </span><b>Broadcast Award.</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> 2024 saw Joe take on sewage companies in</span><b> Joe Lycett vs Sewage. </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">He has also won two </span><b>Royal Television Society awards</b><span style="font-weight: 400;">, a nomination for </span><b>Foster’s Edinburgh Comedy Award</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> for </span><b>Best Newcomer</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (2012). At the </span><b>National Comedy Awards</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> in 2023, he won the</span><b> Comedy Game Changer Award </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">and was nominated for </span><b>Outstanding Male Comedy Entertainment Performance</b><span style="font-weight: 400;">. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Joe has appeared on all of the top comedy entertainment shows including:  </span><b>QI</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (BBC), </span><b>8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (C4), </span><b>Taskmaster</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (Dave/C4), </span><b>Live At The Apollo</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (BBC), </span><b>Michael McIntyre’s Big Show</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (BBC), </span><b>Sunday Night at the Palladium</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (ITV), </span><b>The Graham Norton Show</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (BBC), </span><b>Who Do You Think You Are</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (BBC), </span><b>Have I Got News For You</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (BBC), </span><b>The Big Fat Quiz of The Year</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (C4) and </span><b>The Last Leg</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> (C4).</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">His work as an artist has been featured in the Royal Academy, Manchester Art Gallery, IKON, Birmingham Midlands Arts Centre and Wolverhampton Art Gallery. His portrait of Harry Styles was famously sold to Harry himself for £6 and a KitKat Chunky Peanut Butter.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Joe has released three books </span><b>Parsnips: Buttered</b><span style="font-weight: 400;">, a self-help book designed to teach you how to “baffle, bamboozle and boycott your way through modern life”, released in October 2016. He also released a limited edition book in 2023 called </span><b>Bins</b><span style="font-weight: 400;">, an ode to bins of all shapes and sizes, to raise funds for Queens Heath Pride in Birmingham. All online copies sold out within an hour of going on sale. Joe’s third book, <strong>Joe Lycett’s Art Hole</strong>, which explores his portraits and the scandalous stories behind them, was released in September 2024.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">He has also directed music videos for rising music stars Litany and Katy J Pearson, whilst he has written, directed and produced a series of short films, </span><b>Ray </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">and </span><b>Linda</b><span style="font-weight: 400;">, the former of which toured film festivals around the world.</span></p></div></section><section id="section-Awards" class="tab" data-animation="fadeIn"><div class="infi-content-wrapper"><h2>Awards</h2>

<p><em>“The excellent routines are greatly enriched by Lycett’s manner: playful, laidback, more like on of us, it feels, than the attention-seeking neurotics you might encounter elsewhere.”<br />
</em><strong>The Guardian</strong></p>
<p><em>“What a joy it is to spend an hour with Joe Lycett…Lycett is affable when the tackles the big topics as he is when he deconstructs the trivial. Arenas surely wait.”</em><br />
<strong>The Independent </strong></p>
<p><em>“If he continues this way, Lycett will become one of mainstream’s biggest names.”<strong><br />
</strong></em><strong>★★★★ The Times </strong></p>
